title: Trains to Southport
from: stations across Merseyside and Greater Manchester
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Southport Air Show. Southport is the end of the Merseyrail Northern line, so there are trains in from Liverpool Central every 15 minutes through the day. Sunday times will be confirmed closer to the show. Northern brings you in from Manchester, Bolton and Wigan Wallgate, and both arrive at the same station. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Southport Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot. Head along Lord Street and Nevill Street towards the Promenade and Marine Drive. It’s flat all the way, and you’ll have plenty of other visitors walking with you.
walkBack: Allow about 15 minutes to walk back to the station from Marine Drive, and a bit more when everyone leaves at once after the flying.
tip: Trains get busy through the morning, so I would travel early if you can.
The trains back are very busy straight after the flying. I would suggest a meal in town while the queues clear, as this has worked for me in the past.
Trains no longer run through from Southport to Hunts Cross, so if you’re coming from south Liverpool, you’ll need to change at Liverpool Central.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows journeys from the main stations and city termini around the UK to Southport, with the changes that work well. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 2 November 2026. The big stations and city termini further from Southport use the times for Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. These are this winter’s weekend times, and the summer 2027 times will follow, so please check before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. gaOnly: Merseyrail and Northern, plus a few connections. Merseyrail runs most of the trains here, and Northern brings you in from Greater Manchester through Wigan Wallgate. From London, Avanti West Coast takes you up to Wigan for the Northern train. I’ve only included journeys where the whole trip works on a weekend with sensible changes. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there. I’ve also added eight c2c stations, with the c2c train into London and the connection on from there.

text: If you’re coming from London, you get off the Avanti West Coast train at Wigan North Western, and the Northern train to Southport leaves from the other station in town, Wigan Wallgate. It’s only a few minutes’ walk across the road, and I would follow the signs for Wallgate as you come out.

When I last checked, most Saturday trains gave you between about 25 and 40 minutes from one train to the next, with the walk included, and the Sunday ones a bit longer. The shortest was 11 minutes. That’s still plenty of time for a walk across the road, so there’s no need to rush.

On the way home it works the other way round. Your Northern train gets in at Wallgate and you walk over to North Western for the London train. I would check the departure boards when you get there, as platforms can change on the day.

pay: Look at the show weekend fares
On the 2026 show weekend Merseyrail offered £2 adult and £1 child returns to Southport. I would keep an eye out for the same again in 2027.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.
A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Which station is closest to the show?
Southport. It’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot along Lord Street and Nevill Street to the Promenade and Marine Drive.
How often are the trains from Liverpool?
Every 15 minutes through the day from Liverpool Central. Sunday times will be confirmed closer to the show.
I’m coming from Manchester. What do I do?
Northern runs from Manchester Victoria and Manchester Oxford Road through Wigan Wallgate. If your train ends at Wigan Wallgate, you’ll need to change there.
I’m coming in to Liverpool Lime Street. What do I do?
It’s a short walk from Lime Street to Liverpool Central, where the Southport trains leave from.
Can I do it in a day from London?

You can, but it’s a long day. On the Saturday it takes about 3 hours each way, with a change at Wigan, where you walk across the road from North Western to Wallgate. The Sunday trains are slower, and some of the ones back go through Liverpool. When I last checked, the last train back to London Euston left Southport at 19:02 on the Saturday and 18:03 on the Sunday, so I would check the last train home before you settle in for the afternoon.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
access: Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
Southport station is step free, with level access to the platforms and accessible toilets, and the promenade has ramped, step free access.
